product.name: codespec
promise: Every translation runs against the original.
product.lede: codespec reads a source language into cir/1, a typed JSON model of what code does, rewrites it with passes, and writes Go or Rust from it. A harness compares the original and every output byte for byte. codespec effects maps a Go repository down to the syscalls each function may reach.
product.description: Read code into cir/1, rewrite it, write Go or Rust from it, and compare the original and the output byte for byte on seeded traces.
product.meta: Go, Rust, Java, Groovy and C readers · Go, Rust and C writers · cir/1 JSON Schema · Apache-2.0

art.caption: Generated from examples/greeter: the Go methods, and the Rust codespec writes from them.

sections.title: Reader, passes, writer, harness.
sections.lede: Each step is a program with one job, and every document that crosses between them is validated against the model.

steps.label: read
steps.title: Lift the source
steps.description: A reader adapter, in the language with the best tooling for its source, prints one cir/1 module. The Go reader uses go/types.

steps.label: pass
steps.title: Rewrite and analyse
steps.description: Deterministic, total passes: lookup-guard, then seven facts such as fallible, comma_ok and read_only.

steps.label: write
steps.title: Emit a language
steps.description: The Go writer builds go/ast; the Rust writer builds syn trees. Both read their choices off the facts.

steps.label: harness
steps.title: Prove it behaves the same
steps.description: The original, the Go output and the Rust output run on the same seeded traces; any differing byte fails the run.

sections.title: One definition, checked at every boundary.
sections.lede: The Rust model is the definition of cir/1; the schema, the adapters and every document follow it.

items.title: Strict and canonical
items.description: Unknown fields, unknown kinds, untyped expressions and other formats are refused. One byte sequence per document.

items.title: Refusals, never guesses
items.description: A goroutine becomes a foreign statement with its source and a reason; the Rust writer leaves that function out and lists it.

items.title: Facts computed once
items.description: Writers read shared, fallible, comma_ok, read_only and the rest off the module instead of each deciding for itself.

items.title: Byte-for-byte evidence
items.description: A one-token change planted in the Rust output fails the harness with the seed, the implementation and the first differing line.

items.title: A Rust reader on syn
items.description: Rust to cir/1 to Go, held to the same harness.

items.title: Down to syscalls
items.description: codespec effects reads a Go repository with every package it imports and reports, per function, the syscalls it may reach and the line that leads there.
